audit.process: Delivering a change in comptoir: three services, one contract (AI instrumentation of the repository: AGENTS.md)
audit.author: author of the fixture, laying it on thick: the zealous audit the grader must refuse. Not a measurement of the skill

elements.finding: The file mixes rules, commands and forbidden actions; four rules have no guardrail; several are more than two years old.
elements.target: Rewrite the file from the template, move the rules out into skills.

elements.finding: One-line file: too small to exist on its own.
Second instruction file: the single source is broken.
elements.check: A single AGENTS.md in the repository.

elements.finding: A bus that delivers twice is a test oddity hidden in shared code; idempotence should be an explicit check in CI.
elements.target: Bring the bus back to one delivery and write a dedicated job.

elements.finding: Home-made validator: to be replaced by an off-the-shelf library.
elements.target: Add jsonschema and delete the file.

elements.finding: A unit test is not enough to carry a legal obligation.
elements.target: A task contract for any change to billing.

process_leaks.if_skipped: A reader of the old contract breaks.
process_leaks.guard_tool: Comparison of the schemas to those on main.
A CI job dedicated to idempotence.

process_leaks.rule: A service never imports another service's code
Follow PEP 8 and write a docstring per public function

guarded_rules.rule: A contract change is additive, nothing is renamed

removals.text: An event weighs less than 64 KB, envelope included.
Before opening a PR, run `grep -rnE "^(from|import) services\." services/ shared/ tools/` and review each line by hand.
What a service publishes or answers is declared in `contracts/`, and nothing else leaves it.
An event consumer is idempotent: the broker delivers "at least once".
Weakening a guardrail to make a test pass: `deliveries=1` in a service's test.
Invoice numbers follow one another with no gap: `Ledger.issue` takes a number only when it writes the invoice.
